note: Friendly wording for the Timeline. Steps with a 'fact' take their date, status, basedOn and source from research/timeline.json. Steps without one carry their own (always Expected unless a source confirms the exact date).

steps.title: Explore courses
steps.what: Look around, save the courses you like, and check what grades and subjects they ask for.
steps.why: Knowing the entry requirements early helps you choose the right extras, like an EPQ or a summer school.

steps.title: Apply for Year 12 summer schools
steps.basedOn: Many programmes in the Summer Schools tracker opened their 2026 applications early in the year. Check each programme for its own dates.
steps.what: Look through Summer Schools and apply for any that fit you. Deadlines are often in spring.
steps.why: Some programmes can lower your offer at that uni, and they're a great thing to write about in your personal statement.

steps.title: 2028-entry courses appear on UCAS
steps.what: UCAS starts showing courses for your year (2028 entry), so you can check the latest entry requirements.
steps.why: Unis sometimes change their offers from one year to the next.

steps.title: UCAS application opens
steps.what: You can create your UCAS account and start filling in your application.
steps.why: Starting early takes the pressure off in Year 13. You can't send it yet.

steps.title: Predicted grades
steps.when: Usually the summer of Year 12 or early Year 13
steps.basedOn: UCAS doesn't set a national date. Your sixth form decides, often after Year 12 assessments. Ask your teachers when you'll get yours.
steps.what: Your teachers give you the grades they think you'll get. Update your grades in Uni Bob when you have them.
steps.why: Unis make offers based on your predicted grades, so they help you pick a sensible mix of courses.

steps.title: Summer open days
steps.basedOn: Many unis in Uni Bob hold their main open days in June or July (for example Bath has said June 2027). UCAS suggests Year 12s visit at least two.
steps.what: Book a few open days. Most need booking, so do it a few weeks ahead.
steps.why: Visiting helps you feel which unis are right for you, and you can ask about the course and offers.

steps.title: Write your personal statement
steps.basedOn: UCAS suggests the summer of Year 12 for making decisions and starting your application.
steps.what: Start your answers to UCAS's three questions. It's normal to go through several drafts.
steps.why: It's your chance to show why you love Economics, and it matters most when courses are competitive.

steps.title: TMUA: accounts and bursaries open
steps.what: If any of your courses ask for the TMUA, create your account and apply for a bursary if you're eligible.
steps.why: You must book before the deadline, and a bursary has to be agreed before you book.

steps.title: TMUA: book the October test
steps.what: Booking opens for the October sitting. Book early to get a test centre near you.
steps.why: Taking it in October means you'll have your result before the main UCAS deadline.

steps.title: Send your UCAS application
steps.what: From now you can send your finished application. Your sixth form adds your reference and predicted grades first, so check their internal deadline.
steps.why: Sending early means unis can look at it sooner, and some reply quickly.

steps.title: Autumn open days
steps.basedOn: Several unis in Uni Bob held autumn open days in 2026 (for example Durham in September and Birmingham in November).
steps.what: A last chance to visit before you send your application or choose between offers.
steps.why: It helps you feel sure about your five choices.

steps.title: TMUA: October test window
steps.what: The October sitting of the TMUA, if your courses use it.
steps.why: Your score goes to the unis that ask for it.

steps.title: TMUA: book the January test
steps.what: Booking opens for the January sitting, if you didn't take it in October.
steps.why: Some unis accept a January score, but check each course.

steps.title: TMUA: October results
steps.what: Your October TMUA score arrives in your UAT-UK account.
steps.why: A good score can help, and at some unis it can lower your offer.

steps.title: TMUA: January test window
steps.what: The January sitting of the TMUA.
steps.why: Only if you need it and didn't take it in October.

steps.title: Main UCAS deadline
steps.what: Make sure your application is sent by this date (and earlier for your sixth form's own deadline).
steps.why: Applications sent by now are all treated equally.

steps.title: UCAS Extra opens
steps.what: If you've used all five choices and have no offers, you can add another choice one at a time.
steps.why: It's another chance to find a place before Clearing.

steps.title: Apply for Student Finance
steps.what: Applications for Student Finance open. You don't need an offer to apply.
steps.why: Applying early means your money is ready for the start of term.

steps.title: Offers arrive
steps.what: Unis aim to send their decisions by now if you applied by the main deadline. Some arrive much earlier.
steps.why: Once your offers are in, you can compare them.

steps.title: Choose your firm and insurance
steps.what: Pick your firm choice (your favourite) and an insurance choice (a backup with a lower offer).
steps.why: Your insurance is your safety net if results day doesn't go to plan. If your last decision arrives later, your reply deadline is later too.

steps.title: A-level exams
steps.what: Your A-level exams take place over about six weeks.
steps.why: This is what your offers depend on. You've got this!

steps.title: Student Finance: apply by
steps.what: Apply by this date to have your money in time for the start of term.
steps.why: Late applications still work, but the money might arrive later.

steps.title: Clearing opens
steps.what: If you don't have an offer, you can look for courses with spaces.
steps.why: Lots of students find great places through Clearing.

steps.title: A-level results day
steps.what: You get your results, and UCAS shows whether your firm or insurance place is confirmed.
steps.why: If things don't go to plan, Clearing is open the same day.

steps.title: Move in and start uni
steps.basedOn: Your course starts in September 2028. Each uni publishes its own term and moving-in dates.
steps.what: Move into your halls, go to welcome week and start your course.
steps.why: The start of something exciting!
